narrativeProgression.description: The man introduces the topic: reconstructing the Proto-Indo-European word for 'cuck'.
Explores etymology of 'cuck' in English and Romance languages, highlighting the 'horned' metaphor.
Discusses similar usage in earlier English, suggesting a deeper connection.
Considers possibility of borrowing versus common ancestry, favoring the latter due to sound changes in Germanic languages.
Solidifies argument for common ancestry by showing how 'horn' and its cognates in other Indo-European languages stem from the same root.
Further explores Proto-Indo-European root for 'horn' and its connection to other words.
Reconstructs the Proto-Indo-European word for 'cuck,' explaining relevant morphemes and sound changes.
